summary: Charles Philip Brown was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at East India Company College and Haileybury, and under traditional teachers Velagapudi Kodandarama Panthulu, Venkatasivasastri Tippabhatla, and Advaitabrahmasastri Vatthyam. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1817–1854) and as Professor of Telugu at University College London (~1865–1879).

Charles Ramble works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Durham University and earned his D.Phil. at Oxford in 1981 under Michael Aris. He held posts at Oxford (~2000–2010), EPHE (Director of Studies, 2009), and was president of the IATS (2006–2013).

Charles Rieu was an Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Geneva and the University of Bonn (Doctor 1843) under Christian Lassen, Jean Humbert, Georg Wilhelm Freytag, and Johann Gildemeister. He served as Curator of Oriental Manuscripts at the British Museum and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

Charles Rockwell Lanman specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Yale under William Dwight Whitney and others, and in Berlin, Tübingen, and Leipzig under Albrecht Weber, Rudolf von Roth, Georg Curtius, and August Leskien. He taught at Johns Hopkins (1876–1880) and served as Professor at Harvard University (1880–1926).

Charles S. Prebish is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Case Western Reserve University and under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. His career included serving as Professor of Religious Studies at Pennsylvania State University (~1972–2007) and the Numata Chair at the University of Calgary (2007).

Charles Taliaferro is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College, the University of Rhode Island, Brown University, and Harvard Divinity School, and served as a professor at St. Olaf College from ~1985 to 2022.

Charles Taylor is a philosopher who studied at McGill University (~1949–1952) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1952–1961). He held faculty posts at Université de Montréal (~1961–1974), McGill University as Professor of Political Science (~1961–1998), and Northwestern University (~2002).

Charles Wei-hsun Fu worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1956) and the University of Illinois System (~1965–1969), and held an academic post at Ohio University (~1968–1972).

Charles Wilkins was an Indologist and linguist who studied under the traditional teacher Kalinatha. A co-founder of the Asiatic Society (1784), he served as Oriental Librarian for the East India Company and librarian at the India Office Library and Records (~1801–1836).
Charles Willemen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied under William Reynolds Beal Acker and held a post as professor at Ghent University (attested 1999–2001).

Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin worked in Iranian, Central Asian, Sinological, and Indological studies. He studied law at the University of Liège (~1851–1855) and served as Professor of Oriental Languages and Sanskrit at the Catholic University of Louvain (~1871–1899).

Chatral Sangye Dorje was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under numerous teachers, including Khenpo Ngawang Palzang, Sera Khandro Dewé Dorje, Terchen Dorjé Dradul, and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, whom he later succeeded.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied at Visva-Bharati University, McMaster University, and Magadh University, and served in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Thammasat University (~1973–2000).
Chen Ming is a scholar in Indology, sinology, and history/archaeology. He held a post as Professor at Peking University (attested 2001 and 2013).

Chen-kuo Lin specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at Temple University in 1991 and served as Professor and Distinguished Professor at National Chengchi University (attested 1997–2018), with visiting posts at IIAS and Leiden University.
Cheryl A. Crowley is a scholar of Japanology. She completed her studies under Linda H. Chance, William R. LaFleur, Philip Boas Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.

Chhimed Rigdzin worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Choying Khyabdel, conducted research at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (~1955–1957), and served as Professor of Tibetan at Visva-Bharati University (~1957–1987).
Chhimed Rigdzin Rinpoche was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and held a post at Visva-Bharati University.

Chi Chen Ho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She studied under the traditional teacher Hsuan Hua and earned a Ph.D. in 2010 at the University of California, Los Angeles, under Robert Buswell, where she also worked as a teaching assistant.
Chi-chen Wang was a sinologist who studied at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (~1922–1924) and held a post at Columbia University from ~1929 to 1965.
